title: Deewana
producers: Guddu Dhanoa; Lalit Kapoor; Raju Kothari
character_occupation: Rich man's son; later runs a garage with friends
character_social_background: Wealthy family; son of Ramakant Sahai
role_gist: Raja, the good-hearted son of a rich father, falls for the widow Kajal after knocking down her mother-in-law, and keeps pressing his suit despite her refusals. He defies his father to marry a widow, is thrown out and opens a garage. Kajal comes to love him, and when her presumed-dead first husband Ravi returns she stays with Raja; together the men defeat the villain Dhirendra.
principal_motivation: Marrying Kajal despite her widowhood and his father's opposition
principal_conflict: His father's rejection of a widow bride, then the return of Kajal's first husband and Dhirendra's kidnapping plot
character_arc: Privileged, impulsive admirer becomes a self-supporting husband who wins Kajal's love
character_outcome: Married to Kajal; survives Dhirendra's bomb plot, in which Ravi dies saving them
critical_reception: Positive reviews, with praise for the cinematography, soundtrack and the performances of Bharti and Khan. Nikhat Kazmi (The Times of India) wrote that Khan brought 'fresh zeal' to a clichéd role; Khan later called his own performance 'awful–loud, vulgar and uncontrolled'.
recognition: Shah Rukh Khan's feature-film debut, which won him the Filmfare Best Male Debut award. Regarded as one of the earliest Hindi films about the stigma of widow remarriage; Nadeem–Shravan's soundtrack was a multi-platinum success.
research_notes: Infobox gross of ₹18 crore has no nett/gross label and is not entered. No budget or verdict found.

character_outcome: Marries Mala; Marco ascends to heaven

character_social_background: Newcomer from Darjeeling with no connections in Bombay

Success draws him into the glamorous world of his boss's daughter Sapna, until rivals collapse a bridge he supervised and he is blamed. Disillusioned, he prepares to leave but turns back to Renu.
principal_motivation: Becoming a big engineer
principal_conflict: The lure of wealth and a sabotage that ruins his reputation
character_arc: Ambitious newcomer is seduced by glamour, disillusioned, and returns to his modest love
character_outcome: Reunited with Renu after deciding to leave the rich world

title: Dil Aashna Hai
writers: Imtiaz Hussain (story, screenplay); Hema Malini (story); Iqbal Durrani; Suraj Sanim (dialogues)
source_material: Adapted from the TV miniseries Lace, based on Shirley Conran's novel

principal_conflict: Kidnapping by the thugs of Digvijay Singh and Govardhan Das
character_arc: Devoted helper and rescuer; little personal development documented
character_outcome: Rescues Laila, whose parentage is resolved

principal_conflict: Ashok's contempt for the poor and control over the family
character_arc: Rebels and leaves home, then reconciles with a reformed brother
character_outcome: Reconciled with Ashok

principal_conflict: Maya's mounting debts and ruin
character_arc: Passionate lover who abandons Maya when she is ruined
character_outcome: Deserts Maya, whose disappearance is then investigated

title: Baazigar

title: Darr
character_social_background: Son of Captain Avinash Mehra, Sunil's commanding officer in the Indian Navy
role_gist: Rahul, a naval captain's son, is Kiran's former classmate and obsessively in love with her. He stalks her with calls and visits, befriends her fiancé Sunil to stay close, tries to kill him, and murders the police guarding the newly married couple. He follows them to Switzerland, stabs Sunil and tries to force Kiran into marriage before Sunil shoots him; dying, he begs Kiran not to hate him.
principal_motivation: Possessing Kiran
principal_conflict: Kiran's rejection and her love for Sunil
character_arc: Obsessive admirer escalates to murder and dies expressing shame
character_outcome: Shot dead by Sunil
critical_reception: Widespread critical acclaim for the direction, story, screenplay, soundtrack, cinematography and performances; Khan's portrayal of an obsessive lover was widely appreciated by critics and audiences.
recognition: Won the National Film Award for Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment; Khan was nominated for Filmfare Best Villain. His stammered 'I love you, K-k-k-Kiran' remains iconic, and the film was a career milestone for Deol, Chawla and Khan.
research_notes: The lead calls Darr the highest-grossing Indian film of 1993; the box-office section ranks it third domestically (after Aankhen and Khalnayak) and first overseas. Overseas gross reported as US$500,000 (₹5.58 crore). Budget not confirmed in the fetched text.

title: Kabhi Haan Kabhi Naa
writers: Pankaj Advani; Kundan Shah; Ranjit Kapoor (dialogues)
character_social_background: Son of Vinayak, who despairs of his repeated exam failures
role_gist: Sunil, a happy-go-lucky musician who keeps failing his exams, loves his bandmate Anna, who loves Chris. His lies to split them get him slapped and thrown out of the band, but he wins back his friends and his father's respect. When Chris's marriage is fixed elsewhere Sunil becomes Anna's fiancé, then realises she still loves Chris and reunites them, ending heartbroken but hopeful.
principal_motivation: Winning Anna's love
principal_conflict: Anna's love for Chris and his father's disappointment
character_arc: Jealous schemer learns to put Anna's happiness above his own
character_outcome: Loses Anna to Chris; meets a new girl
critical_reception: Positive reviews; widely considered one of Khan's best performances, and he has called it his favourite film. Sampada Sharma (The Indian Express, retrospective) praised its subtle, circumstantial humour.
recognition: Won the Filmfare Awards for Best Film (Critics) and Best Actor (Critics) for Khan. Premiered in the Indian Panorama of the 24th International Film Festival of India; remade in Telugu as Swapnalokam (1999).

title: Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge
character_social_background: British Indian in London; son of a wealthy, carefree businessman
role_gist: Raj, the brash London-raised son of a carefree businessman, meets the sheltered Simran on a European backpacking trip and falls in love, though she is betrothed to Kuljeet in Punjab. He follows her to India, poses as Kuljeet's friend and wins over her family while refusing to elope without her father's blessing. Thrown out and ambushed, he leaves on a train that Simran boards when her father relents.
principal_motivation: Marrying Simran with her father's blessing
principal_conflict: Baldev's promise of Simran to Kuljeet
character_arc: Carefree flirt becomes a patient suitor who wins the patriarch's consent
character_outcome: Leaves with Simran for London after Baldev relents

recognition: Won ten Filmfare Awards, then a record, including Best Film, Best Director, Best Actor for Khan and Best Actress for Kajol, and the National Film Award for Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment. Showing at Mumbai's Maratha Mandir since 1995, the longest run in Indian cinema. Listed in 1001 Movies You Must See Before You Die and twelfth on the BFI's list of top Indian films.

title: Ram Jaane
source_material: Premise borrowed from Angels with Dirty Faces (1938) and the Bengali film Purushottam (1992)

After Rajiv tries to rape her in Las Vegas, Arjun takes her home, survives a fight with Rajiv's goons, confesses his love and marries her.
principal_motivation: Loyalty to his foster father and protecting Ganga
principal_conflict: Duty to Kishorilal's plan versus Ganga's safety
character_arc: Self-effacing foster son becomes Ganga's protector and husband
character_outcome: Marries Ganga
critical_reception: Mixed-to-positive reviews, praising the soundtrack and the performances of Khan, Chaudhry and Agnihotri but criticising the story and screenplay. India Today cited it as one of the first major Bollywood films to succeed in the United States.
recognition: Twelve Filmfare nominations and three wins: Best Female Debut (Chaudhry), Best Female Playback Singer (Alka Yagnik, 'Meri Mehbooba') and Best Screenplay (Ghai). Released on the eve of the 50th anniversary of Indian independence; remade in Telugu as Pelli Kanuka (1998).
research_notes: The box-office text gives India nett ₹22.83 crore and worldwide ₹40.95 crore, which are entered; its collection table gives nett ₹31.83 crore and worldwide ₹49.95 crore. Overseas US$1.7 million (₹6.12 crore).

title: Dil To Pagal Hai
writers: Yash Chopra; Tanuja Chandra; Pamela Chopra
character_occupation: Director of a musical dance troupe
role_gist: Rahul directs a Mumbai dance troupe and plans a musical, Maya, about a girl waiting for true love. When his friend Nisha is injured he casts Pooja, a gifted dancer linked to him by a recurring tune, and they fall silently in love, though she is engaged to Ajay. Heartbroken, he rewrites the play's ending, until Ajay plays Pooja's taped confession and the lovers declare themselves on stage.
principal_motivation: Finding true love and staging Maya
principal_conflict: Pooja's engagement to Ajay
character_arc: Romantic idealist faces heartbreak and is rewarded with love
character_outcome: United with Pooja
critical_reception: Widespread critical acclaim for its direction, story, screenplay, soundtrack, cinematography and performances. Omar Ahmed (Empire) gave it 4/5; Screen praised a sophisticated film that 'prizes good taste'.
recognition: Three National Film Awards, including Best Popular Film and Best Supporting Actress for Karisma Kapoor. Eight Filmfare Awards, including Best Film, Best Actor for Khan, Best Actress for Dixit and Best Supporting Actress for Kapoor. Listed among the top 10 Yash Chopra films by several outlets.
research_notes: Budget of ₹9 crore includes print and advertising. The infobox gives 30 October 1997; the box-office section says it opened on Friday 31 October 1997, used here. Overseas US$3.3 million (₹12.04 crore). No verdict label found.

title: Duplicate
writers: Robin Bhatt; Akash Khurana; Javed Siddiqui
source_material: Described as a remake of The Whole Town's Talking (1935)
alternate_identity: Double role: the gangster Manu Dada
character_social_background: Devout, mother-loving young man

principal_motivation: Success as a chef and marrying Sonia
principal_conflict: Manu's scheme to take his place and kill him

character_outcome: Marries Sonia after Manu is killed

title: Achanak

research_notes: Budget from the infobox; gross of ₹7.26 crore has no nett/gross label and is not entered.

title: Dil Se..
producers: Mani Ratnam; Ram Gopal Varma; Shekhar Kapur; Bharat Shah
character_social_background: Delhi-based radio journalist whose family arranges his marriage
role_gist: Amar, an All India Radio executive reporting from Assam, becomes infatuated with a mysterious woman he meets at a rain-soaked station. He pursues her to Ladakh and back to Delhi, unaware that Meghna is a suicide bomber planning a Republic Day attack, and falls under CBI suspicion after sheltering her. Escaping custody, he reaches her on parade morning and pleads with her to choose life; as they embrace, her handler detonates the vest.
principal_motivation: Winning the woman he loves
principal_conflict: Meghna's insurgent mission and trauma, and CBI suspicion
character_arc: Curious journalist consumed by love dies with the woman he could not save
character_outcome: Killed with Meghna when her explosive vest is detonated

critical_reception: Mixed. Deepa Deosthalee called it 'a picture-perfect ode to love'; Khalid Mohamed praised the performances, technique and music but found no story; Anupama Chopra (India Today) called it 'a noble attempt' that was not good enough from Mani Ratnam.
recognition: Netpac Award at the 49th Berlinale; National Film Awards for Best Cinematography and Best Audiography; six Filmfare Awards, including Best Music Director (A. R. Rahman) and Best Female Debut (Preity Zinta). First Indian film in the UK box-office top 10; soundtrack sold six million units in India; in Time's 'Best of Bollywood' list (2010). Final film of Ratnam's trilogy with Roja and Bombay.
research_notes: Overseas: US$975,000 in the United States and £537,930 in the United Kingdom. Infobox gross of ₹28.40 crore has no nett/gross label and is not entered. The filmography marks it as Khan's 25th film. No Romances row for Preeti Nair: the summary records only an arranged engagement and one outing.

title: Kuch Kuch Hota Hai
character_occupation: College student; later a widowed father
character_social_background: Widower raising his daughter with his mother's help

Tina dies in childbirth, leaving letters asking their daughter to reunite Rahul with Anjali. Years later young Anjali engineers a meeting at a summer camp, and Rahul rediscovers his love for Anjali, now engaged to Aman, who steps aside at the wedding so she can marry Rahul.
principal_motivation: Love, first for Tina and later for Anjali
principal_conflict: His blindness to Anjali's love, then her engagement to Aman
character_arc: College flirt becomes a widowed father who recognises love in friendship
character_outcome: Marries Anjali

Nikhat Kazmi (The Times of India, 3.5/5) praised Kajol but found the second half 'drowned in a sea of emotions'; Nandita Chowdhury (India Today) called it 'slick, urbane and predictable' but credited Johar with nearly recreating the Khan–Kajol chemistry of DDLJ.
recognition: National Film Award for Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment. Eight Filmfare Awards, including Best Film, Best Director and all four acting awards (Best Actor for Khan). Highest-grossing Hindi film ever overseas until Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham; its soundtrack was the year's best-selling Bollywood album.
research_notes: Box Office India figures via Wikipedia: India gross ₹80.12 crore, nett ₹46.86 crore, distributor share ₹29.88 crore; overseas US$6.3 million (₹26.61 crore); worldwide approximately ₹106.7 crore.

title: Baadshah

recognition: Khan was nominated for the Filmfare Best Comedian award and Amrish Puri for Best Villain.
research_notes: Box Office India figures via Wikipedia; overseas US$1.5 million (₹6.52 crore). The filmography lists the film under 1998 and 1999; release was 27 August 1999.

title: Phir Bhi Dil Hai Hindustani
producers: Shah Rukh Khan; Juhi Chawla; Aziz Mirza
writers: Raaj Kumar Dahima; Manoj Lalwani; Sanjay Chhel

Betrayed by their bosses and politicians, they steal back Mohan's confession, broadcast it before his execution and save him.
principal_motivation: Ratings and scoops, then justice for Mohan
principal_conflict: Media bosses and corrupt politicians
character_arc: Sensationalist reporter becomes a crusading journalist
character_outcome: Saves Mohan; accepts Ria's proposal

research_notes: Box Office India figures via Wikipedia; overseas US$1.67 million (₹7.26 crore). Khan is also a producer.

title: Hey Ram
writers: Kamal Haasan; Manohar Shyam Joshi (Hindi dialogues)
character_social_background: Pathan Muslim who chooses to stay in India after Partition
role_gist: Amjad, a Pathan Muslim archaeologist, works at Mohenjo-daro with his closest friend Saket Ram and resolves to stay in India despite Partition. Years later, sheltering Muslim families in Delhi, he discovers Ram's plot to kill Gandhi and begs him to renounce hatred, revealing that Hindus killed his own father. Struck down by a Hindu mob as Ram tries to shield him, he dies telling police Ram is his brother, turning Ram towards Gandhi.
principal_motivation: Staying in the land he considers home and protecting refugee families
principal_conflict: Communal violence and his friend's radicalisation
character_arc: Steadfast secular friend whose sacrifice redeems Ram
character_outcome: Killed by a Hindu mob
critical_reception: Widespread critical acclaim. T. Krithika Reddy (The Hindu) praised its sound, make-up, cinematography, art and costumes; a review noted that Khan 'as usual comes up with an impeccable performance'.
recognition: India's submission for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film (not nominated). Three National Film Awards, including Best Supporting Actor for Atul Kulkarni. Screened at Toronto and Locarno. Khan's Tamil-language debut; his Dreamz Unlimited distributed the Hindi version.
research_notes: Commercial figures are for the Hindi version: India gross ₹8.91 crore, nett ₹5.32 crore, overseas US$550,000. Infobox budget ₹11 crore; infobox gross of ₹11.3 crore is unlabelled and not entered. Runtime 207 minutes in Hindi, 210 in Tamil. Amjad's wife Nafisa appears only briefly, so no Romances row.

title: Josh

principal_conflict: Gang rivalry with the Bichhoos and Rahul's romance with Shirley
character_arc: Hot-headed gang leader accepts his rival's brother as family
character_outcome: Acquitted; blesses Shirley's marriage to Rahul
critical_reception: Mixed reviews praising the music, cinematography, action and cast but criticising the script. Taran Adarsh (Bollywood Hungama) called it well made with great performances, but found the second half average and the climax weak.
recognition: Five Filmfare nominations, including Best Film and Best Director; IIFA Award for Best Art Direction.
research_notes: No Romances row: Max's love interest Rosanne (Priya Gill, special appearance) does not appear in the plot summary. Overseas US$1.127 million (₹5.01 crore). No runtime in the infobox.

title: Mohabbatein
character_social_background: Former Gurukul student expelled for loving the principal's daughter

He reveals he was once expelled for loving Narayan's daughter Megha, who then killed herself, and vows to spread love in her memory. When the boys face expulsion Raj takes the blame and agrees to leave, until Narayan admits his rules killed his daughter and hands the school to Raj.
principal_motivation: Honouring Megha by bringing love to Gurukul
principal_conflict: Narayan Shankar's regime of tradition, honour and discipline
character_arc: Grieving lover turns mentor and wins his ideological battle

title: Gaja Gamini

Struggling to raise them with help from Geeta, an undercover officer at a drug lord's nightclub, he steals the gangster's money, is framed and suspended. Tracing the conspiracy to the CBI chief and Javed's killer Sawant, he is reinstated and marries Geeta.

recognition: Rights now owned by Red Chillies Entertainment.

title: Aśoka
writers: Santosh Sivan; Saket Chaudhary (screenplay); Abbas Tyrewala (dialogues)
source_material: Based on the early life of the Mauryan emperor Ashoka
character_social_background: Mauryan royal family; grandson of Chandragupta Maurya
role_gist: Prince Asoka, sent away by his mother to escape his half-brother Susima's plots, travels as Pawan and secretly marries Kaurwaki, a fugitive princess of Kalinga. Told she has been killed, he turns brutal, marries the Buddhist Devi, becomes emperor after Susima's death and declares war on Kalinga. Finding Kaurwaki wounded and her brother Arya dying amid the carnage he caused, he throws away his sword and embraces Buddhism.
principal_motivation: Power and survival, then grief-fuelled conquest
principal_conflict: Susima's assassination attempts and the war with Kalinga
character_arc: Ambitious prince turned ruthless conqueror renounces violence
character_outcome: Embraces Buddhism after the Kalinga war
critical_reception: Critically acclaimed abroad (10 of 10 on Rotten Tomatoes). Peter Bradshaw (The Guardian) called it 'a big, brash and deeply enjoyable Bollywood epic'; Variety's David Rooney said Khan 'cuts a dashing figure as a soulful hunk'; the BBC's Santosh Sinha found Khan less convincing in the renunciation.
recognition: Filmfare and IIFA awards for Best Cinematography (Santosh Sivan); Filmfare nominations for Best Film, Best Director and Best Actress (Kareena Kapoor). Released in India as Ashoka: The Great and widely screened abroad.
research_notes: India nett ₹11.54 crore; overseas US$1.8 million (₹8.64 crore). Infobox estimated gross of ₹28 crore is unlabelled and not entered. No verdict found. Khan is also a producer.

title: Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham

Disowned, he moves to London with Anjali and her sister. A decade later his brother Rohan brings the family together, and Yash publicly apologises.
principal_motivation: Duty to his parents and love for Anjali
principal_conflict: Yash's disapproval of a lower-class bride
character_arc: Dutiful son disowned for love and reconciled with his father
character_outcome: Reconciled with Yash; his wedding is belatedly celebrated
critical_reception: Mixed responses from Indian critics, with praise for production values and performances; abroad it scored 12 of 12 on Rotten Tomatoes. Shamaila Khan (BBC, 9/10) praised Khan, Kajol and Kareena Kapoor; Derek Elley (Variety) called it 'highly enjoyable'.
recognition: Led the 47th Filmfare nominations with 16 and won five. The highest-grossing Indian film overseas at the time; regarded as a landmark family drama.
research_notes: Domestic nett ₹550 million; overseas US$8.9 million; worldwide approximately ₹1.36 billion. No Romances row for Naina Kapoor (Rani Mukerji, extended guest appearance): the summary says only that she quietly loves Rahul and steps aside.

character_social_background: Orphan raised by the patriarch Dev Narayan

principal_conflict: His suspicion of Radha and Suraj

title: Devdas
writers: Prakash Ranjit Kapadia; Sanjay Leela Bhansali
source_material: Based on Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay's Bengali novel Devdas (1917)
character_social_background: Aristocratic zamindar family
role_gist: Devdas returns from ten years' study in London and falls in love with his childhood companion Paro, but his mother scorns her lineage and his father humiliates her. Lacking the courage to defy them, he writes that he never loved her, and Paro marries a widowed aristocrat. Devdas sinks into alcoholism, finds refuge with the courtesan Chandramukhi, and dies at the gates of Paro's mansion as they are shut on her.
principal_motivation: Love for Paro, then escape from grief
principal_conflict: His family's class prejudice and his own cowardice
character_arc: Privileged lover destroys himself through drink after failing to fight for love
character_outcome: Dies of liver failure outside Paro's gates
critical_reception: Mixed reviews in India: most praised Madhuri Dixit but criticised Bhansali's direction and the lead performances, though Komal Nahta called Khan 'mind-blowing' and Ratna Rajaiah (The Hindu) called it 'a fabulous, sumptuous, glittering tribute to the lofty ideal of romantic love'.
recognition: India's submission for the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film. One of the few films to win all four top Filmfare awards (Best Film, Director, Actor and Actress). Premiered at the Cannes Film Festival; sets built for ₹200 million.
research_notes: India collections of ₹681.9 million and overseas ₹316.9 million are not labelled nett or gross. Box Office India estimated the Hindi version's total at ₹998.8 million; Wikipedia gives approximately ₹1.68 billion worldwide as of 2003, including a Chinese-language release; hence the range. Premiered at Cannes on 23 May 2002; Indian release 12 July 2002. The four-top-awards claim comes from the Kuch Kuch Hota Hai article.

title: Shakti: The Power
source_material: Remake of the Telugu film Anthahpuram (1998), based on the story told in Not Without My Daughter (1991)

title: Saathiya

research_notes: Yeshwant's protective lie for his wife is a brief marital detail, so no Romances row. Overseas approximately US$925,000 (₹45.2 million).

title: Chalte Chalte
producers: Juhi Chawla; Shah Rukh Khan; Aziz Mirza
character_occupation: Owner of Raj Transport, a small trucking company

principal_conflict: Class and financial pressure within the marriage

critical_reception: Positive reviews praising the theme, screenplay, soundtrack and lead performances; Taran Adarsh called Khan 'an actor par excellence', while some critics noted similarities to Saathiya.
recognition: Last production of Dreamz Unlimited before it became Red Chillies Entertainment. Screened at the Casablanca Film Festival; five Filmfare nominations, including Best Actress (Mukerji).
research_notes: Box Office India figures via Wikipedia; overseas US$2.81 million (₹13.13 crore). Khan is also a producer.

title: Kal Ho Naa Ho
character_social_background: Visitor to New York living with his mother and uncle
role_gist: Aman moves in next door to Naina's struggling family in New York and transforms their lives with his cheer, reviving their café and healing old wounds. Naina falls in love with him, but Aman, secretly dying of a heart condition, pretends to be married and steers her towards her best friend Rohit. He attends their wedding and, on his deathbed, makes Rohit promise that Naina will be his in the next life.
principal_motivation: Making Naina and her family happy before he dies
principal_conflict: His fatal heart condition
character_arc: Life-affirming charmer gives up his own love and dies
character_outcome: Dies after Naina marries Rohit
critical_reception: Critical acclaim for its direction, story, music and performances. Anupama Chopra (India Today) called Advani 'a distinctive voice'; Komal Nahta called Aman one of Khan's best roles; Rama Sharma (The Tribune) found Khan 'overcharged' at times.
recognition: National Film Awards for Best Music Direction (Shankar–Ehsaan–Loy) and Best Male Playback Singer (Sonu Nigam). Eight Filmfare Awards, including Best Actress (Zinta), Best Supporting Actor (Saif Ali Khan) and Best Supporting Actress (Jaya Bachchan); 13 IIFA Awards.
research_notes: Worldwide gross ₹860.9 million from the lead. India earnings of ₹581.8 million are not labelled nett or gross. Filming paused for about six months because of Khan's illness.

title: Yeh Lamhe Judaai Ke
character_social_background: Poor, musically gifted student helped by his friend's industrialist father
role_gist: Dushyant, a gifted but poor student, is helped by his school friend Jaya's industrialist father and grows into a successful musician and Jaya's lover. Manipulated by Nisha and Sujit, he breaks with Jaya, proposes to Nisha and humiliates Jaya, who is then murdered. After learning the truth he confronts Sujit; the killings of the conspirators are finally traced to Jaya's father.
principal_conflict: Nisha and Sujit's scheming
character_arc: Successful musician manipulated into betraying his love
character_outcome: Left with his mentor's reassurance that his love for Jaya was true
critical_reception: Panned by critics and audiences; Taran Adarsh (1/5) likened it to 'watching two films within one film'.
recognition: Largely shot in 1994 and abandoned; completed in 2004 using body doubles.
research_notes: No Romances row and no centrality score: the Wikipedia plot summary is written in a mocking, unreliable tone and mixes 1994 footage with body-double scenes, so the pairing cannot be scored honestly. The filmography spells the character Dushant; the cast list gives Dushyant Kumar.

title: Main Hoon Na

character_social_background: Son of Brigadier Shekhar Sharma, estranged from his stepmother and half-brother
role_gist: After his father dies shielding a general from the rogue ex-commando Raghavan, Major Ram goes undercover as a student at a Darjeeling college to protect the general's daughter Sanjana and reconcile with his estranged stepmother and half-brother Lucky. principal_motivation: His mission and his father's dying wish

title: Veer-Zaara
character_social_background: Orphaned Punjabi Sikh raised by his childless aunt and uncle
role_gist: Veer, an Indian Air Force rescue pilot, helps the Pakistani Zaara scatter her nanny's ashes and falls in love with her, though she is engaged. Called by her friend, he quits the Air Force to bring her away, but agrees to leave for her family's sake and is jailed as a spy by her fiancé Raza. Presumed dead, he stays silent for 22 years until the lawyer Saamiya proves his identity and reunites him with Zaara.
principal_motivation: Love for Zaara and protecting her honour
principal_conflict: Raza's revenge and the India–Pakistan divide
character_arc: Dashing officer sacrifices his freedom and is redeemed by love's constancy
character_outcome: Freed and married to Zaara
critical_reception: Widespread acclaim for its story, dialogue, music, performances and 'sensitive portrayal of India-Pakistan relations' (92% on Rotten Tomatoes; Metacritic 67). Taran Adarsh gave it 4.5/5; Sukanya Verma and Teena Malik criticised its repetition of Chopra formulae.
recognition: Its soundtrack, built on old Madan Mohan compositions, was the year's best-selling album in India.
research_notes: First-run worldwide earnings of over ₹97 crore (lead) and ₹107 crore including re-releases (infobox). India collections of ₹580 million and overseas ₹357 million are not labelled nett or gross.

title: Swades
production_banner: UTV Motion Pictures; Ashutosh Gowariker Productions

principal_motivation: Bringing Kaveri Amma home, then serving the village
principal_conflict: His American career versus his duty to India
character_arc: Detached expatriate becomes a committed citizen
character_outcome: Returns permanently to India

Regarded as a cult classic ahead of its time; Mohan Bhargav reappears in Brahmāstra: Part One – Shiva.

role_gist: Khan appears as the sutradhar, or narrator, of Khalid Mohamed's anthology of three women's stories: Ziya, a rising actress whose mentor-lover refuses commitment; Anushka, a receptionist torn between a wealthy suitor and a colleague who loves her silently; and Rehana, a housewife confronting her husband's affair. The stories converge in an act of female solidarity.
critical_reception: Taran Adarsh (1.5/5) called it an experiment for a very small audience; Sukanya Verma (Rediff.com) found the first story clever and the second predictable.
research_notes: Credited as a special appearance in the filmography and as the Sutradhaar (Narrator) in the cast list. No box-office data.

title: Paheli

character_occupation: Merchant's son on a distant business venture

role_gist: Kishanlal, the dutiful son of a wealthy merchant, leaves his bride Lachchi on their wedding night for a five-year business trip. When the real Kishanlal returns to find her pregnant, a shepherd's test traps the ghost in a bottle, but the ghost escapes and possesses Kishanlal's body.
principal_motivation: Kishanlal: duty to his father's business; the ghost: love for Lachchi

research_notes: India nett ₹187.5 million; overseas US$3.63 million. Infobox gross of ₹320 million is unlabelled and not entered. The cast list names the ghost Mufasaka.

title: Alag

research_notes: Wikipedia says it 'earned only ₹56 lakh', about one-sixteenth of its budget; the figure is not labelled nett or gross and is not entered.

title: Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna
writers: Karan Johar; Shibani Bathija; Niranjan Iyengar
character_occupation: Former professional footballer; junior football coach
character_social_background: New York family man living with his wife, son and widowed mother
role_gist: Dev, a New York footballer, meets Maya by chance on her wedding day just before a car accident ends his career. Four years later he is bitter, jealous of his wife Rhea's success and distant from his son. He and the unhappily married Maya become friends, fall in love and begin an affair. Exposed, they confess, lose their marriages and part, until three years later Maya finds him at a train station.
principal_motivation: Escape from a bitter, failing marriage into love with Maya
principal_conflict: Guilt, family and his own resentment
character_arc: Embittered husband finds love through adultery and lives with the guilt
character_outcome: Divorced; reunited with Maya

research_notes: Worldwide gross ₹113 crore; overseas US$10.56 million; first-week India gross approximately ₹27.85 crore. No verdict label found.

title: Don: The Chase Begins Again

character_social_background: Criminal operating from Kuala Lumpur
role_gist: Don, a ruthless drug-cartel manager in Kuala Lumpur, is wounded fleeing the police, and DCP D'Silva recruits his poor lookalike Vijay to take his place. In the twist ending, Don had recovered, killed Vijay in hospital and swapped places; posing as Vijay he defeats Vardhaan, accepts Roma's love and becomes the cartel's kingpin.
principal_motivation: Power over the drug cartel
principal_conflict: Police, rival lieutenants and Roma's revenge
character_arc: Villain masquerades as his redeemed double and wins
character_outcome: Becomes kingpin of the Asian drug cartel

recognition: Filmfare nominations including Best Film and Best Actor for Khan; Asian Film Award nomination for Best Actor.
research_notes: India gross over ₹710 million; overseas over US$7.8 million; worldwide over ₹1.06 billion (infobox ₹106.34 crore).

title: Chak De! India
character_occupation: Coach of the India women's hockey team; former men's captain
character_social_background: Muslim former national captain ostracised after a loss to Pakistan
role_gist: Kabir Khan, captain of India's men's hockey team, misses a penalty against Pakistan and is branded a traitor through religious prejudice. Seven years later he becomes coach of the neglected women's team, confronts regional rivalries and a revolt led by the veteran Bindiya, and forges 16 players into a unit. The team wins the World Cup in a shootout, and Kabir returns to his ancestral home vindicated.
principal_motivation: Redeeming his name and building a winning team
principal_conflict: Religious prejudice, a hostile federation and a divided team
character_arc: Disgraced player becomes a vindicated coach
character_outcome: Wins the World Cup and returns home with honour
critical_reception: Positive reviews (89% on Rotten Tomatoes; Metacritic 68).
recognition: National Film Award for Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment; five Filmfare Awards including Best Actor (Khan) and Critics Best Film; nine IIFA Awards. The players, dubbed the 'Chak De! Girls', shared the Screen Award for Best Supporting Actress. Named one of India's best films of the 21st century by The Hollywood Reporter India (2025).
research_notes: Worldwide ₹102 crore: India gross ₹85.86 crore (nett ₹66.54 crore) and overseas US$3.94 million (₹15.76 crore). Bindiya's attempt to seduce Kabir is rejected, so no Romances row.

title: Om Shanti Om
writers: Farah Khan; Mayur Puri; Mushtaq Shiekh
alternate_identity: Reincarnated as the superstar Om Kapoor (O.K.)
character_social_background: Chawl-dwelling junior artist raised by his widowed mother; reborn as a film star's son

recognition: Deepika Padukone's Hindi film debut. Asian Film Award for Best Composer (Vishal–Shekhar).
research_notes: India nett ₹794 million after entertainment tax; overseas US$10.15 million; worldwide ₹150 crore (infobox ₹152 crore). No verdict label found. No Romances row for Om Kapoor and Sandy: their bond is limited to the revenge plan and a closing reunion.

principal_conflict: Vijay's plan to sell the house
character_arc: Absent father comes to believe in the ghost and helps free him
character_outcome: Keeps the house after Kailash attains peace

principal_conflict: Taani's inability to love him

recognition: Ten Filmfare nominations, including Best Actor, with wins for Best Male Playback Singer (Sukhwinder Singh, 'Haule Haule') and Best Scene of the Year. Its script was invited into the Margaret Herrick Library of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences. Anushka Sharma's debut; noted as Khan's 50th film.
research_notes: Worldwide gross ₹1,578.9 million; overseas US$8.43 million. Released with limited promotion after the 2008 Mumbai attacks.

title: Luck by Chance

research_notes: Budget ₹150 million from the infobox. Worldwide gross reported in US dollars (US$4,504,365), so not entered in INR columns.

title: My Name Is Khan

character_social_background: Indian Muslim with Asperger's syndrome from Mumbai, living in San Francisco
role_gist: Rizwan, a Muslim man from Mumbai with Asperger's syndrome, joins his brother in San Francisco and marries Mandira, a Hindu single mother. Taking her literally, he crosses America, is detained, reports an extremist, leads hurricane relief in Georgia and meets President Obama before reuniting with Mandira.
principal_motivation: Winning back Mandira by clearing the family name
principal_conflict: Post-9/11 Islamophobia and his wife's grief
character_arc: Literal-minded outsider becomes a national symbol of tolerance
character_outcome: Survives a stabbing, meets the President and returns home with Mandira
critical_reception: Widespread acclaim (86% on Rotten Tomatoes). Taran Adarsh (4.5/5) called it Khan's career-best performance and praised Kajol; Shubhra Gupta (The Indian Express) felt the push to make Rizwan more heroic derailed the film.
recognition: Released worldwide by 20th Century Fox; often called Johar's magnum opus. Khan was honoured at the San Francisco Film Festival in 2017 for the role.

title: Ra.One

Tamil and Telugu versions earned about ₹50 million nett. International premieres began 24 October 2011; India release 26 October. No verdict label found.

title: Don 2

writers: Farhan Akhtar; Ameet Mehta; Amrish Shah

Betrayed by Vardhaan and the hit man Jabbar, he outwits both, negotiates immunity, gets the wounded Roma to an ambulance and exposes the European cartel bosses, emerging as king of the Asian and European underworlds.
principal_motivation: Control of the European underworld
principal_conflict: The European cartel, Vardhaan and Interpol
character_arc: Criminal mastermind carries off the 'perfect crime'
character_outcome: Keeps the real plates and rules both underworlds

research_notes: Production cost ₹760 million excluding Khan's fee. India gross ₹1.06 billion for the Hindi version plus ₹60 million from Tamil and Telugu versions. The article calls it the highest-grossing Bollywood film of 2011, which is not reconciled here. Infobox worldwide estimate of ₹202.81 crore is not entered. Khan is also a producer.

title: Jab Tak Hai Jaan
character_occupation: Indian Army bomb-disposal officer; formerly a street musician and waiter in London
character_social_background: Struggling immigrant in London
role_gist: Samar, a struggling musician in London, falls in love with the heiress Meera, who has vowed to God not to love him; when he survives an accident, she vows never to see him again. Embittered, he joins the Indian Army and defuses bombs without protection, daring God to kill him. Ten years later the filmmaker Akira, who falls for him, reunites him with Meera after a second accident; Meera abandons her vow and Samar proposes.
principal_motivation: Love for Meera and defiance of her God
principal_conflict: Meera's religious vows
character_arc: Carefree lover turned death-defying soldier has love restored
character_outcome: Proposes to Meera in Kashmir
critical_reception: Positive reviews praising Chopra's direction and the leads but criticising the predictable plot; Taran Adarsh gave 4/5 and Shubhra Gupta (The Indian Express) 2.5/5.

research_notes: Worldwide ₹235.66 crore from the lead. The box-office text gives India nett ₹1.02 billion after three weeks (distributor share ₹570 million) and about US$11 million overseas in 13 days.

title: Bombay Talkies
director: Karan Johar; Dibakar Banerjee; Zoya Akhtar; Anurag Kashyap

critical_reception: Positive reviews; Taran Adarsh (4/5) praised the work of four top film-makers in under two hours.
recognition: Released for the centenary of Indian cinema and screened at the 2013 Cannes Film Festival.
research_notes: Infobox gross estimate of ₹10 crore is unlabelled and not entered.

title: Chennai Express

character_social_background: Rich Mumbai bachelor raised by his grandparents

Presented as her lover, he is hunted by her father's men and her intended groom Tangaballi. After fleeing through Tamil Nadu with her and scattering the ashes, he returns to fight Tangaballi and wins her father's consent.
principal_motivation: Escaping trouble, then fighting for Meenamma
principal_conflict: Her father's arranged match with Tangaballi
character_arc: Cowardly bachelor becomes a courageous common man
character_outcome: Wins the right to marry Meenamma
critical_reception: Mixed reviews; Taran Adarsh and Rachit Gupta (Filmfare) each gave it 4/5 as an entertaining masala film.
recognition: Became the highest-grossing Bollywood film worldwide at the time, breaking the record set by 3 Idiots.
research_notes: Final worldwide gross ₹424 crore (US$72.31 million); Box Office India's record-setting figure at the time was ₹396 crore. No verdict label found.

title: Bhoothnath Returns
producers: Bhushan Kumar; Krishan Kumar; Renu Ravi Chopra

role_gist: Khan reprises Aditya Sharma from Bhoothnath in a cameo in this sequel, in which the ghost Bhoothnath, mocked in the ghost world for failing to scare children, returns to India and contests an election with the help of a boy, Akhrot. The sources consulted do not describe Khan's scene.
critical_reception: Taran Adarsh (3.5/5) said it is made with noble intentions and its message resonates in the second half.
recognition: The Election Commission of India urged tax-free status for its voter-awareness message.
research_notes: Collected ₹30 crore in India and ₹2 crore overseas by 20 April 2014 (unlabelled); satellite rights sold for ₹21 crore, which made it profitable for the producers.

title: Happy New Year
character_social_background: Son of a safe designer framed by the tycoon Charan Grover
role_gist: Charlie, a small-time street fighter, spends eight years plotting revenge on the tycoon Charan Grover, who framed his father and drove him to suicide in prison. He assembles a team of misfits and a bar dancer, Mohini, to enter a world dance championship in Dubai as cover for stealing Grover's diamonds from the vault beneath the venue. The heist succeeds, Grover is framed and arrested, the team wins, and Charlie proposes to Mohini.
principal_motivation: Avenging his father
principal_conflict: Charan Grover's power
character_arc: Vengeful loner finds a team and love
character_outcome: Grover is arrested; Charlie proposes to Mohini
critical_reception: Mixed reviews (57% on Rotten Tomatoes): Rajeev Masand gave 2.5/5; Mihir Fadnavis (Firstpost) called it 'Ocean's 11 rewritten by baboons'.
recognition: Record opening day of ₹44.99 crore, the first Bollywood film to reach that figure in a single day.
research_notes: Budget ₹140 crore in the lead, ₹150 crore in the infobox; worldwide gross ₹394 crore in the box-office section, ₹342 crore in the infobox; hence the ranges. No verdict label found.

title: Dilwale
production_banner: Red Chillies Entertainment; Rohit Shetty Productions
alternate_identity: Hides his past as the gangster Kaali
character_occupation: Car tuner in Goa; formerly a gang enforcer in Sofia

Fifteen years earlier he loved Meera, daughter of his father's rival, until their fathers killed each other and she shot him, believing he had betrayed her. When Veer falls for Meera's sister Ishita, the lovers meet again; the truth emerges, and Meera takes a bullet for Raj.
principal_motivation: Protecting Veer, then reclaiming Meera
principal_conflict: Meera's mistrust and the drug baron King
character_arc: Wounded ex-gangster forgives and reunites with his lost love
character_outcome: Reunites with Meera

recognition: Five Filmfare nominations, including Best Actor (Khan) and Best Actress (Kajol); 'Gerua' won Song of the Year at the Mirchi Music Awards. Vinod Khanna's final film.
research_notes: Domestic nett about ₹127 crore after two weeks; worldwide opening weekend ₹130 crore.

title: Fan
alternate_identity: Double role: his obsessive fan and lookalike Gaurav Chandna
character_social_background: Mumbai film star; Gaurav is a middle-class Delhi fan
role_gist: Gaurav, a Delhi fan who resembles the superstar Aryan Khanna, beats up a rival actor as a birthday gift for his idol, but Aryan has him jailed and dismisses him. Heartbroken, Gaurav impersonates Aryan in London and Croatia to destroy his reputation, invades his home and demands an apology. Aryan tracks him to Delhi and subdues him; unwilling to live as anyone but his fan, Gaurav throws himself off a roof, leaving Aryan haunted.
principal_motivation: Aryan: protecting his name; Gaurav: recognition from his idol
principal_conflict: The fan's campaign of revenge
character_arc: Superstar confronts the dark side of fandom
character_outcome: Gaurav dies; Aryan is cleared but haunted
critical_reception: Mixed-to-positive reviews praising Khan's double performance, the visual effects and action but criticising the loose script; Raja Sen (Rediff.com, 4.5/5) called it 'a brilliant film with Shah Rukh Khan at his best'.
recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Special Effects (Red Chillies VFX). Released without songs.
research_notes: India gross ₹120 crore after an 85 per cent second-week drop; overseas over US$10 million. No Romances row: Gaurav's crush on Neha is a minor strand.

title: Ae Dil Hai Mushkil
producers: Hiroo Yash Johar; Karan Johar; Apoorva Mehta
role_gist: Khan makes a cameo as Tahir Taliyar Khan, the ex-husband of Saba, the poet with whom the hero Ayan has an affair, in Karan Johar's drama of unrequited love. The sources consulted identify the role but do not describe his scene.
critical_reception: Mixed reviews praising the direction, music and the performances of Sharma, Kapoor and Rai but criticising the story (53% on Rotten Tomatoes).
recognition: Pritam's soundtrack was an instant success.
research_notes: Budget of over ₹50 crore including marketing and distribution; ₹75 crore recouped from music, satellite and digital rights before release.

title: Dear Zindagi
producers: Gauri Khan; Karan Johar; Gauri Shinde
production_banner: Red Chillies Entertainment; Dharma Productions; Hope Productions
character_social_background: Free-spirited therapist in Goa
role_gist: Jug, an unconventional psychologist in Goa, treats Kaira, a young cinematographer with insomnia who ends relationships before she can be abandoned. Through playful sessions he helps her trace her fears to being left with her grandparents as a child and to see her parents as fallible people. When Kaira admits she has feelings for him, he explains that such feelings are common in therapy, declines a relationship and parts from her warmly.
principal_motivation: Helping Kaira understand herself
principal_conflict: Kaira's fear of abandonment
character_arc: Steady guide who holds professional boundaries
character_outcome: Ends the therapy; Kaira reconciles with her parents and moves on
critical_reception: Positive reviews (73% on Rotten Tomatoes). Namrata Joshi (The Hindu) wrote that 'the chemistry between Bhatt and Khan makes the film sparkle'; Shubhra Gupta (The Indian Express) found it boiler-plate; Andy Webster (The New York Times) called it 'a resounding victory'.
recognition: Filmfare nominations for Best Actress (Bhatt) and Best Lyricist (Kausar Munir).
research_notes: Released 23 November 2016 in North America and 25 November worldwide. No Romances row: Kaira's feelings for her therapist are treated as transference and declined, and Jug has no romantic function.

title: Raees
producers: Ritesh Sidhwani; Farhan Akhtar; Gauri Khan
writers: Rahul Dholakia; Harit Mehta; Ashish Vashi; Niraj Shukla
source_material: Reported to be based on the criminal Abdul Latif, which the makers denied
character_social_background: Poor Muslim boy from Fatehpur, Gujarat
role_gist: Raees, a poor boy in prohibition-era Gujarat, rises from running liquor for the bootlegger Jairaj to building his own empire with political protection, locked in a long duel with the honest ACP Majmudar. He marries his neighbour Aasiya and wins an election, but, ruined by political betrayal, agrees to smuggle 'gold' for Musabhai that turns out to be explosives used in bombings. He kills Musabhai, surrenders and is shot by Majmudar.
principal_motivation: Wealth, standing and serving his community
principal_conflict: ACP Majmudar and political betrayal
character_arc: Resourceful bootlegger becomes a community leader and dies atoning for an unwitting role in terror
character_outcome: Shot dead by Majmudar after surrendering
critical_reception: Positive reviews for Khan and Siddiqui: Taran Adarsh (4/5) praised the cat-and-mouse chase; Rajeev Masand (3/5) said Khan 'commands your attention'; Sarit Ray (Hindustan Times, 2/5) credited its Muslim protagonists.
recognition: Five Filmfare nominations, including Best Actor. Its soundtrack drew over 1.6 billion YouTube streams; the most pirated Hindi film of 2017.
research_notes: Budget ₹91 crore in the box-office text, ₹87 crore in the infobox; distributor share ₹67.3 crore. No Romances row: the marriage to Aasiya is a single sentence in the summary. Mahira Khan's only Hindi film.

title: Tubelight

critical_reception: Mixed-to-negative reviews (27% on Rotten Tomatoes): Anupama Chopra called it 'cinema as a sermon'; Raja Sen (NDTV) gave it 1/5.

title: Jab Harry Met Sejal
character_social_background: Emigrant from Nurmahal, Punjab, who failed to become a singer in Canada

Their bickering turns into love, but Harry, feeling unworthy, will not say so and she flies home. He follows her to India, finds her wedding called off, and they decide to marry and visit his family.
principal_motivation: Escaping loneliness and guilt
principal_conflict: His sense of unworthiness and Sejal's engagement
character_arc: Rootless cynic finds love and returns home
character_outcome: Engaged to Sejal and reunited with his family
critical_reception: Mixed-to-negative reviews criticising the direction, story and Sharma's performance but praising the music, cinematography and Khan. Anupama Chopra wrote that Khan 'is still Raj'; Hindustan Times called it lethargic. Imtiaz Ali later rated it 3 out of 10.
recognition: IIFA Award for Best Male Playback Singer (Arijit Singh, 'Hawayein'); several Mirchi Music Awards for 'Hawayein'.
research_notes: Worldwide ₹153.43 crore (India ₹89.4 crore, overseas ₹64.1 crore; US$10 million overseas). Khan's lowest opening in three years.

title: Zero
production_banner: Colour Yellow Productions; Red Chillies Entertainment
character_social_background: Man with dwarfism from a wealthy Meerut family
role_gist: Bauua Singh, a brash man with dwarfism from Meerut, falls for Aafia, a scientist with cerebral palsy, but abandons her and later flees their wedding to meet the film star Babita, for whom he goes to work. Realising his wrong, he pursues Aafia to New York, learns she had been pregnant, and is rejected. He volunteers for a mission to Mars, declares his love as she arrives for the launch, and returns to Earth fifteen years later.
principal_motivation: Proving his worth, first to himself and then to Aafia
principal_conflict: His immaturity and Aafia's rejection
character_arc: Insecure man-child redeems himself through an impossible sacrifice
character_outcome: Reaches Mars, is lost in space and survives to return fifteen years later
critical_reception: Mixed reviews (31% on Rotten Tomatoes) praising the visual effects, Khan's energy and Kaif's career-best performance but criticising the second half; Rajeev Masand gave 2/5.
recognition: Filmfare nominations including Best Actor (Khan) and Best Supporting Actress (Kaif). Cameos by Salman Khan, Sridevi, Kajol, Rani Mukerji, Deepika Padukone and others.
research_notes: Domestic gross ₹87 crore and overseas US$14 million (Box Office India); worldwide ₹191 crore.

research_notes: UAE release 19 September 2019; India release 20 September.

The story is framed as a televised interview in which Narayanan recounts his career; the sources consulted do not describe Khan's scene.

critical_reception: Mixed-to-positive reviews (69% on Rotten Tomatoes); Sonil Dedhia (News18, 4/5) singled out 'a crackling Shah Rukh Khan cameo'.

character_occupation: Scientist and member of the Brahmānsh

principal_conflict: Junoon's gang

recognition: First instalment of the planned Astraverse trilogy.

title: Pathaan
role_gist: Pathaan, a RAW agent recovering from a mission, forms a unit of retired agents and pursues Jim, a former RAW agent turned mercenary who plans to release a mutated smallpox virus on India. He allies with the ISI agent Rubai, who betrays him in Moscow; rescued from a prison train by Tiger, he later tracks the virus with Rubai to Siberia and Afghanistan, kills Jim in a mid-air fight over Delhi and is reinstated as head of the unit.
principal_motivation: Protecting India
principal_conflict: Jim's bioterror plot
character_arc: Sidelined agent is vindicated and reinstated
character_outcome: Kills Jim and becomes head of JOCR
critical_reception: Generally positive reviews (85% on Rotten Tomatoes): Taran Adarsh (4.5/5) called it a 'complete entertainer'; Sukanya Verma (Rediff.com, 4/5) praised Khan's 'weathered intensity, grizzly charisma and trademark wit'.
recognition: First Hindi film to gross ₹100 crore worldwide on its opening day and the first original Hindi film to net over ₹400 crore domestically. Fourth instalment of the YRF Spy Universe.
research_notes: Worldwide gross is the infobox estimate of ₹1,050.30 crore. No Romances row: the summary describes Pathaan and Rubai's alliance and betrayal but no stated romance. No verdict label found.

title: Jawan
alternate_identity: Double role: his father, Captain Vikram Rathore
character_occupation: IPS officer and women's-prison jailer (Azad); army commando (Vikram)
character_social_background: Born in prison to a mother later executed; father framed as a traitor
role_gist: Azad, a prison jailer, leads a gang of women inmates in heists that expose corruption, from farmer suicides to a hospital's oxygen shortage, while marrying Narmada, the officer hunting him. He is the son of Captain Vikram Rathore, framed as a traitor by the arms dealer Kalee and presumed dead, and of Aishwarya, executed after giving birth in prison. Azad finds his amnesiac father alive, and together they defeat and hang Kalee.
principal_motivation: Clearing his father's name and delivering justice to the oppressed

character_outcome: Kalee is hanged; Azad takes on a new mission

recognition: Record opening-day net of ₹75.4 crore in India across versions; became the highest net-grossing Hindi film in India, overtaking Pathaan. Filmfare nominations including Best Film and Best Actor. Atlee's Hindi debut.
research_notes: Worldwide gross over ₹1,148.32 crore as of 10 November 2023 (infobox ₹1,150 crore). No verdict label found.

title: Tiger 3
role_gist: Khan reprises Pathaan in a cameo in the fifth YRF Spy Universe film, helping Tiger escape after he is sentenced to death. Taran Adarsh singled out the cameo in his review.
critical_reception: Mixed reviews (55% on Rotten Tomatoes); Taran Adarsh (4/5) appreciated Khan's cameo.
recognition: Record Diwali opening day for a Hindi film (₹94 crore worldwide).
research_notes: Gross figures as of 15 December 2023.

title: Dunki
production_banner: Jio Studios; Red Chillies Entertainment; Rajkumar Hirani Films
writers: Rajkumar Hirani; Abhijat Joshi; Kanika Dhillon

role_gist: Hardy, an ex-soldier, comes to a Punjab village to repay a debt to Manu's late brother and vows to get her and her friends to England. When visas fail he leads them on the perilous illegal 'donkey flight', but refuses to claim false persecution in a London court and is deported while the others stay. Twenty-five years later he brings the terminally ill Manu back to India through a ruse, confesses his love and proposes before she dies.
principal_motivation: Repaying a debt and keeping his promise to Manu
principal_conflict: Visa barriers and his refusal to disown India
character_arc: Principled soldier loses and finally brings home the woman he loves
character_outcome: Manu accepts his proposal and dies
critical_reception: Mixed reviews (48% on Rotten Tomatoes); critics praised Khan and Pannu, but Uday Bhatia (Mint Lounge) said the film uses migration as an occasion for grandstanding.

research_notes: India ₹262.25 crore (Hindi nett ₹212.42 crore); overseas ₹208.35 crore; worldwide ₹470.6 crore. No verdict label found.
